settings.combination: maximum; duplicate records never add strength (polygon area fractions of one source layer are summed per cell, capped at 1)
settings.note: Authored spawning suitability, not measured discovery probability. Evidence tiers, kernels, survey-density normalisation and host-rock priors are documented in docs/remaining-ore-evidence.md (section 'v2 evidence model').

major.meaning: USGS Major Mineral Deposits of the World entry (world-class or nationally significant)

deposit_large.meaning: specialist-compilation deposit with tonnage/grade or a producing mine in a national resource inventory

deposit.meaning: specialist-compilation deposit or mine without size, documented deposit boundary

prospect.meaning: specialist-compilation prospect, potash drill-hole/structure, coal sample site

mrds.comment: MRDS records: peak by development status x MRDS score. MRDS 'score' is the USGS estimate of how much information a record holds (A most, E least), used here as a documentation-quality proxy, not deposit size.

surveyDensity.comment: Applies to MRDS records only. Kernel radius is widened by (effortReference / window records)^sparseRadiusExponent up to maxRadiusKm where surveys are sparse. Enrichment = local share of the commodity among all MRDS records in a window / its global MRDS share, with pseudo-counts; the multiplier is clipped to [floor, 1]. In densely surveyed regions incidental mentions of a commodity no longer saturate, while a lone record in a sparsely surveyed region keeps its full tier weight. An additional effort damping lowers low-tier MRDS weights where the window holds very many records.

polygons.comment: Cell value = weight x (minimumFractionWeight + (1 - minimumFractionWeight) x covered fraction). Invalid polygons are repaired with shapely.make_valid; MultiPolygons are split; parts spanning > 180 degrees of longitude are unwrapped to 0..360 and rasterised modulo 360.

priors.comment: Low-weight host-rock and climate priors written only to the POTENTIAL plane. Lithology is the dominant 0.5-degree GLiM class (geology-grids-v1.json). Codes: 2 vb basic volcanic, 4 pb basic plutonic, 6 sc carbonate, 7 va acid volcanic, 8 mt metamorphic, 9 pa acid plutonic, 10 vi intermediate volcanic, 13 pi intermediate plutonic, 14 ev evaporite.

lithology.why: carbonate platforms host Mississippi-Valley-type Pb-Zn and fluorite
mafic/ultramafic plutonic rocks host chromite, Ni-Cu-PGE sulfides and Ti-V magnetite
basic volcanics host volcanogenic massive sulfide and basalt-hosted copper
intermediate/acid volcanic and intermediate plutonic arcs host porphyry Cu-Mo-Au and epithermal Au-Ag
granites host greisen/vein Sn-W, granite-related U and fluorite

graniteAureole.why: metasediments/sediments within one cell of a granite cell (contact aureole, greisen and skarn Sn-W)

metamorphic.why: orogenic gold is hosted almost exclusively in metamorphic terranes; graphite in graphitic schist/gneiss

crystallineGold.why: metamorphic terrain within one cell of granite or mafic rocks (orogenic gold in greenstone/schist belts; graphitic schist)

bauxite.why: lateritic/karst bauxite forms by intense humid-tropical weathering of most bedrock types; unconsolidated cover, evaporites, ice and water excluded

peat.why: peat accumulates where precipitation exceeds evapotranspiration on flat, poorly drained ground: boreal/temperate lowlands and humid tropical coastal/fluvial lowlands. Climate = earthdata 0.25-degree sea-level-equivalent mean temperature and VS rainfall (aridity based); relief = median 2-arc-minute roughness and mean elevation from the same bake.

authoredBestGuess.comment: Registry entries with tierRule 'authored' (docs/research/remaining-ores-2026-09-29/corrections/authored/best-guess-districts.csv): districts/basins authored for this project from general knowledge of world mining geography where no openly licensed survey layer is on disk. Best guesses, not survey data. Peak by size x confidence, never above the deposit_large tier (0.85) and so always below USGS Major Deposits (0.95); kernel radius per entry (point 40-75 km, district 45-120 km, basin 50-150 km; at least the MRDS producer radius because authored positions carry 10-30 km uncertainty) with the normal kernel floor; observed plane only, no depth.

caveats: 0.5 degree cells and tiered point kernels (25-75 km) are gameplay inference, not deposit footprints.
Tiers, density normalisation and priors reduce but cannot remove geographic survey-coverage bias; the main point source (USGS MRDS) remains US-heavy.
Potential-plane priors from 0.5-degree dominant GLiM lithology and climate are low-weight geological permissiveness, not observed evidence.
Coal and peat remain regional where no global inventory is on disk (see docs/remaining-ore-evidence.md for the recommended datasets).

Deep evidence boosts only at/under its reported depth; depths are used only when a source states them (coal polygons, potash sites with K_DEPTH_M, reviewed gypsum). Assessment-tract depth ranges are not deposit tops and are not used.
V1 file format keeps the strongest deep weight paired with its own burial depth (shallower wins ties); weaker shallow records can be omitted, never used to expose stronger deep evidence early.
